assume that $U_1 R=S_1^{-1} U_1$ and $G V_2= V_2S_2$

issues.failure_explanation: The left hypothesis contains the dimensionally meaningless term $S_2A_2$ (should involve $U_1$), and even with $U_1$ the equation $S_1^2U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+U_1A_2=0$ is not what the displayed transformation $(I+zX(S_1-zI)^{-1}U_1)A(z)$ requires: cancelling the poles at the eigenvalues of $S_1$ requires $U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2=0$, i.e. $U_1$ is a left eigen-block of $A(z)$ for the eigenvalues of $S_1$, and it is those eigenvalues (not those of $S_1^{-1}$) that are removed, since $\det(I+zX(S_1-zI)^{-1}U_1)=\det S_1/\det(S_1-zI)$. Theorem th5's hypothesis $U_1R=S_1^{-1}U_1$ and the Section 3 use with $S_1^{-1}=\Lambda_{R,1}$ and equation (10) are consistent only with the corrected version, so the theorem as stated is internally inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem with hypothesis $U_1A_0+S_1U_1A_1+S_1^2U_1A_2=0$ and with the eigenvalues of $S_1$ (not $S_1^{-1}$) moved to infinity, consistently with Theorem th5 and with the Section 3 verification.
issues.overall_effect: The stated hypothesis of Theorem th3.2 is not what Section 3 verifies via (10); the stated set of eigenvalues moved to infinity (eigenvalues of $\Lambda_{R,1}$) are not even eigenvalues of $A(z)$. The intended application in Section 3 matches the correct theorem, so no later result is lost once the statement is fixed.
issues.title: Recalled block-shift theorem is misstated (left hypothesis and moved eigenvalues inconsistent with the transformation and with Theorem th5)
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and forced by the surrounding consistent usage; all downstream results survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem th3.2 requires $\det S_1\ne0$, and the transformation uses $(S_1-zI_q)^{-1}$ with $S_1=\Lambda_{R,1}^{-1}$. The standing assumptions allow $\lambda_{2m}=\infty$, giving $R$ (hence $\Lambda_{R,1}$) an eigenvalue $0$, so $S_1$ does not exist and the theorem cannot be invoked; this occurs in Example 1 ($\lambda_8=\infty$) and in every QBD with singular $A_2$. Hence the deflated polynomial $\widetilde A(z)$, its coefficient formulas, and the factorization (eq:facat) with $\widetilde G,\widetilde R$ are not justified in that regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the block-shift theorem in terms of $\Sigma_1:=S_1^{-1}$ (possibly singular), writing the left factor as $I+zX(I-z\Sigma_1)^{-1}\Sigma_1U_1$ with hypothesis $\Sigma_1^2U_1A_0+\Sigma_1U_1A_1+U_1A_2=0$, and note that the coefficient formulas and Theorem th5 go through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation that $\bar G,\bar R$ solve the barred QMEs (used in Theorem thm:added-1 and hence in the reduced equations (eq:qmeGbar), (eq:qmeRbar)) lacks justification whenever some $\lambda_i=\infty$, including Example 1.
issues.title: Block shift applied with $S_1^{-1}=\Lambda_{R,1}$ although $\Lambda_{R,1}$ may be singular (infinite eigenvalues allowed, e.g. Example 1)
issues.why_classification: The reformulation is a routine rewriting of the same computation; all claims and the advertised scope (including infinite eigenvalues) survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the left invariant subspace corresponding to the eigenvalues in the open unit disk of the sought solution $R$ is approximated by the span generated by the rows of $U_{2,2}^{(k)}$
$T_{R,1}\in \mathbb{R}^{(m-\ell)\times m}$ formed by the last $m-\ell$ rows of $T_R$

issues.failure_explanation: With $A_2^{(k)}=U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$, the approximate left null space of $A_2^{(k)}$ (the rows $t$ with $tA_2^{(k)}\approx0$) is spanned by the transposes of the last columns of $U_2$, i.e. the last rows of $U_2^\top$, not the last rows of $U_2$. Taking $T_R=U_2^{(k+1)}$ and $T_{R,1}$ as its last rows gives $T_{R,1}A_2^{(k)}=(\text{last rows of }U_2)U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$, which is not small in general, so $T_{R,1}$ does not approximate the left invariant subspace of $R$ and the returned $\Lambda_{R,1}$ is meaningless; the same misassignment appears in the text partition of $U_2^{(k)}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set $T_R=(U_2^{(k+1)})^\top$ and partition $(U_2^{(k)})^\top$ (equivalently, use the last $m-\ell$ columns of $U_2^{(k)}$ transposed) throughout Section 4 and Algorithm alg:isg.
issues.overall_effect: As written, Algorithm alg:isg does not deliver its $T_R$/$\Lambda_{R,1}$ output contract, and the downstream $\bar A_i$ (which need $T_{R,1}\widetilde A_2=0$) and $R$ in Algorithm alg:gfull would be wrong.
issues.title: Left invariant subspace of $R$ taken from rows of $U_2^{(k)}$ instead of rows of $(U_2^{(k)})^\top$
issues.why_classification: A single local correction restores the intended construction with no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: has eigenvalues $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$, each with multiplicity 2, and $\bar{G}_{11}$ is the only solution to \eqref{eq:qmeGbar} with eigenvalues $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$

issues.failure_explanation: The pencil $(M,N)$ has each $\mu_i$ as a double eigenvalue. $Z_{21}Z_{11}^{-1}$ is the sought solution only if the leading $\ell\times\ell$ diagonal blocks $(T_{11},S_{11})$ carry each $\mu_i$ exactly once (and $Z_{11}$ is nonsingular). An unordered QZ decomposition may place two copies of some $\mu_i$ (and omit another $\mu_j$) in the leading block, in which case $Z_{21}Z_{11}^{-1}$ is not $\bar G_{11}$ and need not be a solution at all. The algorithm contains no reordering/selection step, so its output guarantee is not delivered as written.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a reordering step (e.g. ordered QZ) so that the leading $\ell$ generalized eigenvalues are $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_\ell$, one copy each, and require $Z_{11}$ nonsingular.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:QZ, and hence step 3 of Algorithm alg:gfull, is underspecified; correctness depends on an unstated ordering of the Schur form.
issues.title: Algorithm alg:QZ does not specify the eigenvalue ordering of the generalized Schur form
issues.why_classification: A standard local addition to the procedure fixes the gap without affecting any result.

issues.failure_explanation: The coefficients $B_i$ in (eq:Bbar) already contain $\bar A_{122}^{-1}$ and are computed before the nonsingularity test; if $\bar A_{122}$ is singular the algorithm has no branch for $\bar G_{21},\bar R_{12}$ yet still executes the final step using them, so it is ill-defined. Nonsingularity of $\bar A_{122}=T_{R,1}(A_1+A_2G)W_{G,1}$ is a compression of the nonsingular matrix $A_1+A_2G$ and is not shown to follow from the Section 2.2 assumptions; the paper only reformulates it as nonsingularity of $T_{R,1}A_0W_{G,1}$ (when $\Lambda_{G,1}$ is nonsingular) and leaves it as an unverified condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove that $T_{R,1}(A_1+A_2G)W_{G,1}$ is nonsingular under the standing assumptions, or add its nonsingularity as an explicit hypothesis of the algorithm/statements and move the test before the computation of the $B_i$ with a documented failure exit.
issues.overall_effect: The input–output contract of Algorithm alg:gfull (compute $G$ and $R$ under the Section 2.2 assumptions) is not established; the algorithm is undefined on an uncharacterized subset of admissible inputs.
issues.title: BS-CR requires $\bar A_{122}$ nonsingular but neither guarantees it nor handles the singular case
issues.why_classification: Resolving it needs either a new nontrivial lemma or an added hypothesis that narrows the advertised scope by an uncharacterized amount; the method otherwise survives.

The uniqueness of $G$ and $R$ implies that $A(\mu_i)$ has a kernel of dimension 1

issues.failure_explanation: In Case 3 the values $1$ and $-1$ each appear twice among $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_8$, so $G_{11}=\mathrm{diag}(\mu_i)$ and $R_{11}=G_{11}^{-1}$ each have a double eigenvalue $\pm1$ and $A(z)=(zR-I)P(zI-G)$ has $\pm1$ as eigenvalues of multiplicity 4 with $\dim\ker A(\pm1)\ge2$. This contradicts the stated claim of multiplicity 2 and violates the distinctness/kernel-dimension assumptions of Section 2.2 (and the uniqueness of $\bar G_{11}$ used by Algorithm alg:QZ), so Case 3 is not a test within the paper's framework, contrary to the presentation.
